subject: Mathematics
learning_objectives: Recognize and identify numbers from 1 to 10
Count objects up to 10 accurately using one-to-one correspondence
Write and sequence numbers from 1 to 10
Match written numerals with the correct quantity of items
introduction: Welcome students to the world of numbers. Begin by showing ten fingers and counting together from 1 to 10 with a cheerful counting song. Explain that numbers help us count everything around us like pencils, toys, and friends.
teacher_activity: Hold up large number flashcards (1 to 10) one by one and pronounce the number name clearly.
Place physical counting counters (beads/blocks) on the table and count aloud with the class.
Draw sets of simple shapes on the blackboard (e.g., 3 stars, 5 circles) and write the corresponding numeral next to them.
Guide students to trace numbers in the air with their index fingers.
student_activity: Echo the teacher in pronouncing number names from 1 to 10.
Clap hands while counting: 1 clap for 1, 2 claps for 2, up to 10 claps for 10.
Count their own fingers and school supplies on their desk.
Trace numbers on their notebooks and slate boards.

lesson_steps.title: Warm-up & Number Song
lesson_steps.description: Sing a short counting rhyme (1, 2, buckle my shoe / 1 to 10 finger count) to engage the class.

lesson_steps.title: Numeral Recognition (1 to 5)
lesson_steps.description: Introduce numerals 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 with flashcards and physical items.

lesson_steps.title: Numeral Recognition (6 to 10)
lesson_steps.description: Introduce numerals 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 with counting beads and board illustrations.

lesson_steps.title: Interactive Counting Practice
lesson_steps.description: Call volunteers to the front to count objects in a basket and point to the matching number card.

lesson_steps.title: Review & Recap
lesson_steps.description: Count together from 1 to 10 forward and backward as a whole group.

classroom_activities.description: Draw numbers 1 to 10 on the floor. When the teacher calls out a number, the student jumps onto the correct number circle.
Students work in pairs. One student shows a number card, and the other student collects that exact number of crayons.

assessment_questions.question: How many fingers do you have on one hand?

homework.title: Home Counting Detective
tasks: Count 5 spoons and 3 cups in the kitchen with your parents.
Draw 4 flowers and 6 stars in your notebook and write the numbers below each drawing.
Practice writing numbers 1 to 10 two times.
